title: Smith Street reconstruction award and new reserve policy
subtitle: Board appointments for the new economic development corporation, transit study, naloxone for firefighters, technical rescue agreements, golf course servicing and heritage designations.
overview: Council awarded the Smith Street and Victoria Crescent reconstruction in Elora to Sousa Concrete and directed staff to look for separate funding for a proposed parkette {{vote:m12}}. Work is expected to start this construction season, with the contractor setting the schedule. Smith Street will be local access only while it is under way.

Council appointed five public members to the first board of the Centre Wellington Economic Development and Tourism Municipal Services Corporation {{vote:m3}}. It also adopted an updated Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy {{vote:m13}} and endorsed the Transit Feasibility Study {{vote:m5}}. Staff will next meet the County about shared services and grant funding.

Centre Wellington Fire Rescue will receive free naloxone kits from public health {{vote:m9}} and can offer technical rescue services to neighbouring municipalities on a cost-recovery basis {{vote:m10}}. Council also rezoned a West Garafraxa property to prohibit residential uses {{vote:m11}}. Through the consent agenda it approved heritage designation notices for two Fergus properties and an Environmental Protection Officer appointment {{vote:m7}}. After closed session, the board appointments were the only matter reported. The meeting also recognized the Fergus Whalers as Schmalz Cup champions.

decisions.item: Smith Street and Victoria Crescent reconstruction
decisions.detail: Council awarded Tender #43-26 to Sousa Concrete at $1,777,490.28 including contingency and excluding HST, and directed staff to explore funding options for the proposed parkette.
Council appointed five public members, three for three-year terms and two for two-year terms, to the board of the new Municipal Services Corporation.
Council adopted the updated policy and authorized staff to make the related transfers between reserves for 2026.
Council endorsed the study and directed staff to publish the Notice of Study Completion.
Council received an update on the servicing strategy and the Environmental Assessment Addendum study notice for the redevelopment, for information.
Council authorized the Managing Director of Community Services to sign an agreement for naloxone kits from Wellington-Dufferin-Guelph Public Health.
Council authorized agreements to provide technical rescue services to neighbouring municipalities and let the Fire Chief finalize operating procedures.
Council approved terms of reference for a joint committee with the Wellington County municipalities for the 2026-2030 term and directed that establishing and appointing by-laws be executed.

debate: On the golf course servicing study, a councillor asked why the study area had grown. Staff said the developer now proposes a plan of subdivision with municipally owned water and wastewater systems instead of a condominium. Staff said this triggers source water protection work and a review of where treated wastewater would be discharged.

Councillors asked about the possible number of housing units, whether municipal communal systems outside the urban boundary are a precedent, and staffing and financial effects. Staff said no applications were filed yet, called this a one-off, and said connecting to existing services is preferred. They said costs will be reported back. One councillor questioned why the item was on the consent agenda.

On Smith Street, councillors asked whether the lowest bid was the best choice. Staff cited the contractor prequalification process and the contractor's comparable past projects. Other questions covered detours, parking and a point of contact for residents, since County work on Geddes Street may overlap. One councillor hoped the parkette would return to council if funding falls short.

On the reserve policy, a councillor asked why the municipal accommodation tax reserve covers only tourism. Staff said legislation limits the funds to tourism. The CAO said more detailed policy would come with the 2027 budget. Another councillor thought the WSIB reserve looked small, and staff agreed to investigate and report back.

A development company's delegate supported designating a heritage home on its Fergus lands. The company had withdrawn its earlier plan to demolish it after hearing from the local heritage committee. Councillors welcomed the decision. The company said the current tenant supports the plan and can stay as long as desired.
